title: How would you migrate master data from a legacy system to a custom cloud-based solution (API design, cloud storage, ETL migration, DB setup, monitoring, security, CI/CD)?
shortTitle: How would you migrate master data from a legacy system to a custom cloud-based solution
keyPoints: Profile the legacy data first: find nulls, duplicates, encoding problems, and dirty formats before designing the transform.
Stage in cloud object storage (S3/GCS) as a durable, replayable landing zone so failures do not require re-reading legacy.
The ETL pipeline: extract from legacy, transform (clean, validate, map codes), load into cloud DB in idempotent batches.
Idempotent loads via upserts keyed on legacy ID so re-running never creates duplicates.
Reconciliation and parallel run prove correctness: compare counts and balance totals, run both systems side by side.
Security: TLS in transit, KMS encryption at rest, least-privilege IAM, PII masking in non-production.
CI/CD: migration code is tested and automated, not a hand-run script on someone's laptop.

s1_definition.oneliner: Extract, transform, load, reconcile, and parallel-run, treating the migration as idempotent, secure, observable, and automated rather than a one-shot copy.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **Data profiling** – Analyze legacy data for nulls, duplicates, encoding issues, and dirty formats before designing the transform.
- **Staging zone** – Cloud object storage (S3/GCS) as a durable, replayable landing area so failures need not re-read legacy.
- **ETL pipeline** – Extract from legacy, transform (clean, validate, map old codes to new), load into the cloud database.
- **Idempotent load** – Upserts keyed on a stable legacy ID so re-running updates instead of creating duplicates.
- **Reconciliation** – Compare record counts and balance totals between source and target to prove correctness.
- **Parallel run** – Serve reads from the new system while validating against the old before cutting over writes.
s1_definition.analogy: National Bank of India is moving from an old paper-and-mainframe records room to a new digital vault in the cloud. You photograph each record (extract), correct smudges and reformat to the new filing standard (transform), file neatly in the new vault (load), and keep the old room open to compare both for a while (parallel run) until the new vault is verified perfect.

sections.s6_takeaway:
Migrating master data from a legacy system to the cloud is a controlled ETL pipeline with reconciliation, not a one-shot copy. Start with data profiling to understand the legacy mess: duplicate customers, inconsistent date formats, balances as comma-separated strings. Stage the export in cloud object storage as a durable, replayable landing zone so failures never require re-reading the fragile legacy system.

The transform cleans, validates, and maps old codes to new ones. The load is idempotent via upserts keyed on legacy ID, so an interrupted migration re-runs safely without creating duplicates. Reconciliation compares record counts and balance totals between source and target, and you run both systems in parallel before cutting over writes, always with a rollback plan.

At National Bank of India, Pankaj migrated 1.5 million customer records. An earlier attempt without idempotent loads created duplicate Rajesh rows on restart. After adding upserts, checkpoints, and nightly reconciliation comparing total balances, the migration proved clean at every step. Security wrapped everything: TLS in transit, KMS at rest, PII masked in non-production, and the entire migration was tested and deployed through CI/CD.

Remember one sentence: master data migration is an idempotent, reconciled ETL pipeline that stages in cloud storage, cleans and validates on the way in, proves itself by matching counts and balance totals, and runs the old and new systems in parallel before cutover.
